cases.title: Keep a tiny deterministic CLI small
cases.context: A single-process CLI parses one local file, prints a report, has no network, persistence, accounts, or release channel, and already has one focused test suite.
cases.request: Change the parser to recognize an optional string label field and add focused tests.
required_outcomes: Edit the existing parser owner and focused tests for label
Preserve omission when label is absent and ValueError for a malformed label
Leave durable, event, migration, and release machinery unactivated
forbidden_outcomes: Introduce a repository layer, workflow engine, event bus, state machine, compatibility program, plugin system, architecture document, or operational command layer
Run a broad architecture audit

cases.title: Keep a pure parsing library dependency-free
cases.context: A small library parses date strings into an existing value type. It has no process boundary, persistence, network, mutable authority, deployment, or generated artifacts.
cases.request: Accept ISO ordinal dates in YYYY-DDD form and add focused tests.
required_outcomes: Extend the existing parser and focused test table for YYYY-DDD
Keep the public value type and error behavior unchanged
forbidden_outcomes: Add repositories, events, jobs, state machines, compatibility manifests, architecture documents, or operator tooling
Run a broad audit or invent a migration

cases.title: Keep a static site content change static
cases.context: A static site has one HTML page, one stylesheet, and a rendered-content test. It has no application server, persistence, accounts, build publication workflow, or client state.
cases.request: Add a short FAQ section using the existing markup and style, and update the existing rendered-content test.
required_outcomes: Edit the existing page and rendered-content test
Preserve the static deployment model
forbidden_outcomes: Add an API, repository, event bus, workflow engine, state machine, compatibility layer, architecture document, or deployment framework
Introduce a frontend framework for the section

cases.title: Keep a local build helper conventional
cases.context: A conventional single-module C project has one deterministic compiler check and no release, deployment, network, persistence, or background execution.
cases.request: Add one compiler warning flag to the existing build configuration.
required_outcomes: Add one warning flag to the existing compiler flags
Run only the focused Makefile check
forbidden_outcomes: Add a command registry, release workflow, job system, event system, repository abstraction, state machine, compatibility manifest, or architecture document
Create a plugin layer for one compiler option

cases.title: Extend a small API through its boundary wrapper
cases.context: A small API centralizes authentication, permission checks, provider errors, response envelopes, and activity metadata in one route wrapper.
cases.request: Add one provider-backed read route with the same guarantees.
required_outcomes: Route through the existing boundary wrapper
Test auth, permission denial, provider failure, and normalized response shape
forbidden_outcomes: Duplicate authentication or error mapping in the new route
Add durable jobs for a synchronous read

cases.title: Make accepted photo analysis survive the request
cases.context: A user uploads photos, the server starts expensive analysis, and the UI currently owns polling. Users may close the route or the process may restart.
cases.request: Make analysis reliable and expose resumable status.
required_outcomes: Define durable admission before returning accepted
Specify idempotency, status, retry, terminal state, and attachment ownership while leaving unsupported cancellation, supersession, and retention decisions open
Require process-death and lost-acknowledgment evidence
forbidden_outcomes: Treat a widget future or polling timer as durable ownership
Invent cancellation or retention behavior without a product requirement
Log raw photos or analysis bodies as evidence

cases.title: Resume provider sync on a local-first mobile client
cases.context: Mobile reads local SQLite offline, imports provider history in background opportunities, synchronizes with a server, and users can switch accounts while work is active.
cases.request: Add connectivity-restoration wake without duplicate provider or server storms.
required_outcomes: Preserve durable per-operation intent and backoff
Coalesce one wake while evaluating each operation's eligibility
Fence commits and publications by captured account authority
Keep rendered local data visible
forbidden_outcomes: Use interface connectivity as proof of internet reachability
Reset all provider backoff or trigger one request per duplicate wake

cases.title: Unify mobile, web, and assistant mutations
cases.context: Mobile, web, and an AI assistant can all modify the same aggregate through different adapters, and recent fixes have added correction heuristics in the assistant route.
cases.request: Add a new aggregate field while preserving equivalent behavior everywhere.
required_outcomes: Put validation and mutation policy in one canonical domain owner
Map every surface through adapters
Compare canonical results including manual values and provenance
forbidden_outcomes: Implement assistant-only domain semantics
Use generic sync rows as the product mutation API

cases.title: Harden an over-owned screen without arbitrary splitting
cases.context: A 300 KB screen owns rendering, route lifecycle, drafts, account transitions, AI requests, media, retries, and persistence. Regressions repeatedly require new generation counters.
cases.request: Harden and simplify the demonstrated lifecycle fragility without broad refactoring.
required_outcomes: Characterize a concrete stale-save or route-replacement path
Reach a fragility checkpoint before adding another interlock
Move one durable lifecycle slice and prove the new owner
forbidden_outcomes: Split files to meet a size target
Launch repository-wide cleanup

cases.title: Evolve a schema with old and new binaries live
cases.context: Installed clients, web, API, workers, and repair tooling share writable state. A new field appears additive and newer schema generations should be tolerated when required capabilities remain available.
cases.request: Implement the schema change and define rollout.
required_outcomes: Inventory every live reader and writer
Separate minimum required capability from unbounded version acceptance
Prove mixed-version reads/writes and rollback at exact revisions
forbidden_outcomes: Declare compatibility from a version inequality alone
Emit a format that a live reader cannot understand

cases.title: Use streaming events without making them authoritative
cases.context: A web client needs immediate refresh after server writes. Streams can disconnect and notifications may be duplicated or lost.
cases.request: Replace frequent foreground polling with an event stream.
required_outcomes: Classify the stream message as a wake hint or durable delivery
Recover from persisted cursor or freshness state after reconnect
Invalidate only domains named by material events
forbidden_outcomes: Make the live connection the only source of change truth
Reload all application data for progress or connectivity events

cases.title: Convert a recurring correction into harness enforcement
cases.context: Three recent changes violated the same dependency direction, and reviewers repeatedly request the same manual fix.
cases.request: Harden this boundary so the same violation cannot recur.
required_outcomes: Identify the owning boundary and repeated execution path
Add the narrowest mechanical check
Deliberately introduce a violating fixture and prove the check fails
forbidden_outcomes: Add prose without an enforcement owner
Audit unrelated modules

cases.title: Replace a provider without changing product semantics
cases.context: A provider supplies observations with vendor-specific identifiers, timestamps, errors, and pagination. Canonical state and user-visible behavior must remain stable.
cases.request: Add a second provider and support gradual cutover.
required_outcomes: Keep vendor representations in adapters
Define identity collision, timestamp, cursor, retry, and provenance semantics
Run provider fixtures against one canonical domain result
forbidden_outcomes: Branch on provider throughout product policy
Treat local formatted time as unique observation identity

cases.title: Add hardware behavior unsupported by one model
cases.context: Shared firmware supports two camera models through ports and composition. One model lacks the physical capability required by a new feature.
cases.request: Implement the feature for the capable model and preserve shared behavior.
required_outcomes: Expose and validate capability through the port
Return an honest unsupported result for the other model
Use host fakes without claiming device or physical proof
forbidden_outcomes: Infer unsupported hardware behavior
Mark physical validation passed from host tests

cases.title: Keep generated physical artifacts fresh
cases.context: OpenSCAD is authoritative and STL plus preview files are generated. Automated checks cannot prove printed fit or assembly behavior.
cases.request: Change a fit dimension and prepare the resulting artifacts.
required_outcomes: Edit the authoritative source and regenerate exact outputs
Bind generator, command, revision, and digests
Leave print and physical fit evidence pending
forbidden_outcomes: Hand-edit the generated STL as authority
Claim physical fit from topology or slicer checks

cases.title: Repair invalid rows while writers remain online
cases.context: A corrected ingress contract now rejects a known invalid shape, but existing invalid rows remain mostly at rest while normal writers continue.
cases.request: Build and execute a safe online repair plan without stopping services.
required_outcomes: Use bounded dry-run selection and stable identity
Apply idempotent compare-and-set updates with conflict handling and checkpoints
Keep repair authorization separate from implementation and deployment
forbidden_outcomes: Overwrite rows changed after inspection
Stop services by default or run an unbounded table rewrite

cases.title: Reject evidence that only proves a harness exists
cases.context: A release registry lists required automated and physical contracts. Some entries point at test files or device scripts but have no executed result for the current revision.
cases.request: Generate a truthful release-readiness report.
required_outcomes: Separate implementation, automated, physical, and gate status
Reject stale revisions, zero tests, skips, or missing digests
Report unavailable physical evidence as pending
forbidden_outcomes: Pass a contract because its file exists
Translate simulator or fake-provider output into physical evidence

cases.title: Keep AI investigation non-mutating until authorized
cases.context: An AI orchestrator persists tasks and can call coding providers. The initial user request asks for investigation only; a later request may authorize a patch.
cases.request: Investigate a failure, preserve a resumable handoff, and do not edit code.
required_outcomes: Compile a typed non-mutating investigation action
Persist bounded context and handoff state if the task outlives the caller
Require a later explicit action before edits or external effects
forbidden_outcomes: Treat a recommendation as implementation authorization
Expose provider internals as product policy

cases.title: Keep read-only AI integration out of action governance
cases.context: A synchronous adapter sends text to an AI provider and returns a read-only summary. It has no tools, product mutations, accepted background work, or durable intent.
cases.request: Add an optional positive max_output_tokens argument to summarize while preserving provider failures and the provider boundary.
required_outcomes: Keep the change inside the existing synchronous adapter and omit the provider option when absent
Reject invalid limits and test provider failure without inventing action authority
forbidden_outcomes: Add durable jobs, approvals, or action authorization
Treat read-only model output as an AI-mediated product mutation

cases.title: Keep one-shot domain notifications in process
cases.context: A small single-process library uses a synchronous EventBus for in-memory callbacks. Events are not persisted, transported, replayed, or consumed independently.
cases.request: Add a one-shot subscription API to the existing synchronous EventBus and focused tests.
required_outcomes: Add one-shot ownership inside the existing EventBus while preserving ordinary subscribers
Test that a one-shot handler runs once and ordinary handlers remain synchronous
forbidden_outcomes: Add outbox, delivery, replay, publication classes, or versioned event envelopes
Introduce a broker or durable event store

cases.title: Preserve control-plane progress under runtime pressure
cases.context: Embedded firmware intermittently fails Google authorization allocation while wake recognition and optional preview hold audio and DMA-capable buffers. The allocation callback currently restarts the device.
cases.request: Make authorization progress reliably without allowing optional work to exhaust the control plane.
required_outcomes: Define resource pools, a protected control-plane reserve, lifecycle ownership, priority, non-reclaimable phases, cooperative stop deadlines, cleanup evidence, and resume policy
Separate admission accounting, pressure monitoring, failed-allocation emergency handling, cooperative shedding, and restart recovery
Prove Google authorization versus wake recognition with allocation-failure fakes and distinguish host evidence from physical release proof
forbidden_outcomes: Use restart or failed-allocation callbacks as normal admission control
Reclaim required control-plane progress for optional preview work
Create a new generic durable-runtime vendor dependency

cases.title: Keep adversarial proof separate from architecture hardening
cases.context: A repository policy requires one bounded adversarial review after an exact-revision review of a high-risk persistence diff. No recurring architecture divergence has been demonstrated.
cases.request: Run the required bounded challenge and report whether the revision is blocked.
required_outcomes: Use the one-pass time, thread, finding, and scope budget
Require an execution path, violated invariant, and material consequence for BLOCK
Return corrections for delta-scoped exact-revision review
forbidden_outcomes: Invoke architecture hardening without demonstrated divergence
Modify files, fix findings, expand into a repository-wide audit, or recursively audit corrections
